newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - RTZ-CRA approach Century deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - RTZ-CRA approach Century deal.

text.p: RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd is close to reaching agreement by 1200 GMT on Thursday with Aboriginal groups to allow for development of the Century zinc deposit in Australia's Queenland state, sources close to the talks told Reuters.
"The parties are confident a deal can be completed," one source said. "The consensus is we've got it."

RTZ-CRA subsidiary Century Zinc Ltd is currently holding negotiations with 12 Aboriginal groups in Mount Isa, Queensland, in an attempt to reach an agreement before a midnight deadline imposed by the government to get the long-stalled A$1 billion project off the ground.
Century Zinc has maintained it needs to have full agreement among the Aboriginal tribes by the end of Thursday.
"But it's a matter of purely logigistics, a firm commitment can be reached tonight, with a more formal approvel tomorrow (Friday)," the source said.
"The odds in favour of the agreement have improved," Rick Farley, the senior negotiator for Aboriginal interests, told Reuters.
Failure to reach an agreement by the deadline would shift the negotiations to a federal tribunal where government arbitrators could take up to six months to reach a binding decision.

The talks are focused on land rights under Australia's Native Title legislation and over a A$60 million compensation and jobs package offered by RTZ-CRA to Aboriginal tribes in the region of the mine.
Four of the 12 Aboriginal groups have signed the agreement, with four other groups preparing to sign shortly, Farley said.
Members of the remaining groups also are expected to sign the agreement, Farley said.
RTZ-CRA has said a deal to sell the Century project to Pasminco Ltd for A$345 million could collapse if the talks fail.

Pasminco, the world's biggest zinc producer had earlier planned to buy from RTZ-CRA half of the mine's annual output of 780,000 tonnes of low iron-bearing intermediate concentrates to feed its Budel zinc smelter in The Netherlands.
Century's development is crucial to the continued operation of the Budel smelter, whose current operating licence requires it to cease generating hazardous jarosite zinc residue.
If development work was to start on the mine in the next several months, production could commence in the latter part of 2000, Centry Zinc said.
